title: Simulated Global Radar — 2-Day Forecast
abstract: A worldwide forecast of where rain, snow and thunderstorms will be falling over the next two days. The colours are the ones you already know from a weather radar map: blues and greens for light precipitation, yellows and oranges for heavy rain, reds for the most intense cores. Hover anywhere to read the value in dBZ — the decibel scale radar meteorologists use for how strongly precipitation reflects a radar beam. Nothing here was measured by an actual radar. The field is what a radar *would* see if one were parked at that spot, computed from a global weather model that resolves weather systems at about 28 km. At that scale the model represents storms statistically rather than one at a time, so expect broad, smooth precipitation shields rather than individual thunderstorms — the large-scale picture is reliable, a single cell on the map is not. Updated every six hours, hourly out to two days.
